title: MoQT Codec Test Vector File
description: A collection of codec test vectors pairing hex-encoded wire bytes with expected decoded representations or errors.

message_type.description: The message type or codec unit being tested (e.g., 'varint', 'subscribe', 'client_setup').

message_type_id.description: Hex-encoded message type ID from the wire format (e.g., '0x03' for SUBSCRIBE).

spec_section.description: Reference to the specification section defining this message type (e.g., '9.7').

id.description: Unique identifier within the file. Kebab-case.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this case tests.

hex.description: Lowercase hex-encoded wire bytes. No 0x prefix, no separators.

decoded.description: Expected decoded representation as a plain JSON object.

canonical.description: Defaults to true. Set to false for valid-but-non-canonical encodings (decode-only test).

error.description: Error category for invalid vectors. Names the kind of complaint a conforming decoder must make, not the specific error it raises: there is more than one defensible way to notice most of these, and a vector is evidence about the protocol rather than about a particular parser. incomplete: The frame ended early. Nothing about the bytes present is wrong; there are not enough of them. unknown_message: The frame begins with a type code this version assigns to nothing - a control message, a data stream or a datagram. invalid_type: The type code is inside the form the version defines and is one the version separately names as invalid, such as a reserved bit combination. Distinct from unknown_message, which is about a code no table assigns at all. invalid_value: A field holds a value the version does not allow it. invalid_parameter: A parameter is wrong in itself: its type, its length, its value's range, or its position in a delta-coded run. parameter_out_of_scope: A parameter is well formed and appears in a message its own definition does not name. Only versions that require a receiver to reject it use this; earlier ones say such a parameter is ignored, and there is nothing to assert. duplicate_parameter: A parameter type appears twice where the version forbids repeating it. missing_parameter: A parameter the message requires is absent. payload_not_permitted: An object carries a payload where its status or its framing leaves no room for one.

error_detail.description: Optional human-readable detail about the expected failure.

profiles.description: Which conformance profiles this vector's expectation binds. Omitted means both. 'endpoint' is a consumer bound by every rule the specification states for a receiver; 'forwarder' is one that carries bytes between endpoints and is bound only by what it must parse to find where a frame ends. A vector asserting that bytes MUST be refused can be true of the first and not of the second, and a corpus that cannot say so makes the second fail tests it was never meant to pass. A consumer runs the vectors naming its profile and should count what it leaves out rather than passing over it quietly: a profile is a claim about which rules apply, not a way to make a failing vector go away.
